sections.content: You found a vacant house. The lawn is overgrown, the mail is piling up, and the property screams motivated seller. The only problem? You have no idea how to reach the owner. That is exactly where skip tracing comes in. Skip tracing is the process of locating a person's current contact information — phone numbers, email addresses, and mailing addresses — using public records and data aggregators. For real estate investors, it is one of the most powerful tools in your prospecting toolkit. If you are just getting started building your lead machine, check out our [How to Find Motivated Sellers: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/finding-motivated-sellers) for the full picture.
Why Skip Tracing Matters for Real Estate Investors

Most of the best real estate deals never hit the MLS. They come from absentee owners, tax-delinquent landlords, probate heirs, and people going through financial hardship who need to sell quickly. The challenge is that many of these owners are hard to find. They may have moved, changed phone numbers, or simply never updated public records. A quality skip tracing service bridges that gap, giving you accurate contact information so you can make a direct offer before anyone else even knows the property is available.

For example, imagine you are working in [Detroit, MI](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/detroit-mi) — a market loaded with tax-delinquent and vacant properties. You pull a list of 200 absentee owners from county records, run them through a skip tracing service, and come back with phone numbers for 160 of them. You make calls, and three of those owners are ready to sell at a steep discount. That is a realistic outcome when you combine good data sources with a reliable skip tracing tool.
What to Look for in a Skip Tracing Service
Not all skip tracing services are created equal. Before you spend money on a subscription or a bulk upload, there are several key factors worth evaluating.

items: Hit rate: The percentage of records that return a valid contact. Look for services with 80% or higher hit rates on real estate-specific lists.
Data freshness: Old phone numbers are worthless. The best services update their databases regularly — some as frequently as every 30 to 90 days.
Cost per record: Pricing typically ranges from $0.05 to $0.25 per record for bulk uploads, or $0.50 to $1.50 per individual lookup. Volume discounts matter if you are running large lists.
Data sources: The best services pull from multiple databases including credit bureaus, utility records, voter registration, and USPS data.
Integration: Does the service plug into your CRM, dialer, or list management tool? Automation saves hours of manual work.
Customer support: Especially important when you are running large batches and something goes wrong.

sections.content: The Best Skip Tracing Services for Real Estate Investors
1. BatchSkipTracing

BatchSkipTracing is widely considered the industry standard for real estate investors. Their bulk upload pricing starts at around $0.18 per record, and they are known for solid hit rates and clean data. They offer same-day turnaround on most batches, which is critical when you are trying to move fast on a hot list. Their interface is simple — you upload a CSV, map your columns, and download results within hours. They also integrate with several popular CRMs.
2. PropStream

PropStream is more than a skip tracing tool — it is a full property data platform that includes skip tracing built in. At around $99 per month, it gives you access to property records, owner data, comps, and skip tracing credits. For newer investors who want everything in one place, it is a strong all-in-one option. You can learn more about pulling free baseline data before upgrading to a paid tool in our guide on [How to Pull Property Data From County Records for Free](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/free-property-data-county-records).
3. REISkip

REISkip is a newer entrant that has gained popularity for its competitive pricing and high accuracy on mobile numbers specifically. Their plans start around $0.15 per record in bulk, and they offer a free trial with 50 records so you can test the data quality before committing. If you are working in competitive markets like [Memphis, TN](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/memphis-tn) or [St. Louis, MO](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/st-louis-mo) where absentee owner lists are large, the cost savings add up fast.
4. TLO (TransUnion)

TLO is a professional-grade skip tracing platform used by law enforcement, private investigators, and some high-volume real estate investors. The data quality is excellent, but access requires a business account and compliance vetting. It is not the easiest to get started with, but for investors running thousands of records per month, the accuracy and depth of information make it worth it.
5. Spokeo and BeenVerified

These consumer-facing tools are fine for one-off lookups, but they are not built for bulk real estate investing. At $2 to $5 per search, the cost becomes prohibitive quickly if you are working any meaningful volume. Use them when you need to verify a specific contact or do a quick manual lookup, not as your primary skip tracing solution.

Always clean your list before uploading it to a skip tracing service. Remove duplicates, standardize address formatting, and verify that owner names match county records. A clean input list consistently produces better hit rates — sometimes improving results by 10 to 15 percentage points.
How to Build a Skip Tracing Workflow That Gets Results
Having a great skip tracing service is only half the battle. The real power comes from building a repeatable system around it. Here is a simple four-step workflow that works well for most investors.

items: Step 1 — Build your list: Start with a targeted property list. Tax-delinquent owners, absentee landlords, and pre-foreclosure properties all make excellent skip tracing candidates. Our article on [Tax Delinquent Property Lists: A Hidden Source of Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/tax-delinquent-property-list-guide) walks through exactly how to pull these lists.
Step 2 — Run the list: Upload your cleaned CSV to your skip tracing service of choice. Most return results within a few hours for batches under 1,000 records.
Step 3 — Prioritize contacts: Sort results by those with mobile numbers first, since mobile contacts convert at significantly higher rates than landlines in real estate outreach.

Step 4 — Make contact: Use a combination of cold calling, texting, and direct mail to reach out. Not every channel works for every seller, so diversifying your outreach improves overall response rates.

sections.content: Once you start getting responses and negotiating deals, run your numbers before making any offer. Use our free [Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to quickly figure out your maximum allowable offer based on ARV, repair costs, and your target profit margin. Making an offer without running the numbers first is one of the most common mistakes newer investors make. The money in real estate is made in the finding, not the closing. If you can consistently locate and contact off-market property owners before your competition, you will always have deals in your pipeline — regardless of market conditions.
Common Mistakes to Avoid with Skip Tracing

items: Skipping list quality: Garbage in, garbage out. A poorly sourced list will waste your skip tracing budget regardless of which service you use.

Ignoring compliance: Skip tracing data must be used in compliance with the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) and other applicable regulations. Always consult a legal professional before launching large outreach campaigns.
Only calling once: Most successful investor contacts happen on the third to fifth attempt. Build a follow-up sequence and stick to it.
Not tracking results: Monitor your hit rate, contact rate, and conversion rate by list type. Over time, this data tells you which lead sources are worth your skip tracing budget.
